name: Simplex Castings Ltd
title: Simplex Castings Ltd - 513472 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: H1 FY27 revenue ₹124 crore (+23%) and PAT margin ~11.7% with FY27 ₹300 crore reiterated, but railway mega-order slipped and FY28 capacity ramp is back-end loaded.

summary.headline: Simplex Castings Q2 FY27 revenue rose 13.71% to ₹63.01 crore, with EBITDA up 32.12% to ₹12.75 crore and margin at 20.23%; FY27 guidance held at ₹300+ crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest quarterly PAT, at ₹7.64 crore (up 36.98% YoY), with PAT margin at 12.13%. H1 revenue rose 23.21% to ₹123.96 crore and H1 EBITDA rose 29.05% to ₹24.26 crore (margin 19.58%). Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹300+ crore, which implies roughly 50% growth over H1, and guided H2 at about 40:60 split between Q3 and Q4. Working capital is the main constraint until preferential issue proceeds (about ₹100 crore) come in, and capacity expansion in the fabrication shop is partly delayed to Q4 FY27 and beyond.

segments.name: Cocon doors / steel plant castings
segments.commentary: Management says Simplex holds about 90-95% share in current cocon battery castings across steel plants; four to five batteries underway in India, with four more batteries planned next year (Bokaro, Durgapur, two for Bhilai/IISCO). Each battery is about ₹25-30 crore, roughly ₹120 crore of cocon doors in total.

segments.name: Railways (castings and fabricated items)
segments.commentary: Management expects a mega wagon-bogie order (about 1 lakh wagons over 2.5-3 years, roughly 30-35k wagons) to slip from the July-September window to next quarter. Plan B covers couplers, suspension tubes and other regular railway castings, and fabricated loco and metro bogies, with a target of 30-40% of business from railways.

segments.name: Power and fabrication
segments.commentary: Management targets over ₹150 crore of heavy power-plant structure turnover, and fabrication-shop capacity is to rise from 500 to 1,500 tons per month for structures and from 200 to 350 tons per month for equipment after the new sheds are complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹300+ crore reiterated; management said October and half of November were running ahead of H1 pace. Implied H2 is about 50% above H1.
H2 quarterly split guided at about 40% in Q3 and 60% in Q4.
EBITDA margin for H2 expected to be broadly similar to H1 (about 19-20%). Management said PAT margins should be sustained at 8-10%, versus a historical range of 7-8%.
FY28 revenue target of ₹500 crore, with the current capacity plus railway orders stated as sufficient. Current capacity expected to be utilised at 80-90% by next year.
Capex of ₹25 crore planned, split ₹25 crore capital and working capital; the working capital requirement is expected to rise as the company moves towards ₹500 crore.
capex_capacity: Fabrication shop: three new sheds planned; two expected to be completed in FY27, with commissioning guided to Q4 FY27 rather than Q3. Management said about 50% of the project spills into the next FY.
Fabrication structures capacity to rise from 500 to 1,500 tons per month; equipment capacity from 200 to 350 tons per month after machines and sheds are added.
Covered area to rise to about 50-60% of 15 acres (currently 20-25% used), with heavy cranes to be installed.
Foundry and CNC machine shop on a separate 15-acre site already operational; casted bogie development is under way.
Management said the company is not yet using the new sheds for FY27 volumes; existing facilities can produce the guided volumes.
demand_pricing: Order book of about ₹150 crore pending, with a further ₹100+ crore in pipeline; the majority is expected to execute in FY27.
Management described the current margin cycle as the best seen in 40 years and driven by niche cocon door and spares orders, but said sustained margins above 10% would be difficult.
Other expenses fell as smaller castings are now outsourced rather than made in-house.
Fabrication orders are short-cycle (1.5-2.5 months); equipment orders take 4-7 months. Management called the order book short-term, with an average of 3-4 months.
Export of fabricated structures is limited; management cited Brazil cocon door orders (two batteries) as an export opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹300 crore FY27 guidance intact, and what is the H2 margin outlook given H1 commodity inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹300+ crore target is on track and H2 margins should be broadly similar to H1 (about 19-20%). It cited seasonal H2 strength and price-variation clauses in long-term orders.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~₹60 crore gap to ₹330 crore be bridged, and how is working capital being funded until the preferential issue comes in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has registered on TReDS-type bill discounting platforms to monetise receivables. It cited a ₹150 crore order book plus ₹100 crore pipeline as coverage, and said the preferential issue will fund working capital.

qa_highlights.question: When will the capex in CWIP be commissioned, and will it affect FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the capex is due in March 2027 and part will spill over by about five to six months. Management said FY27 guidance is not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Has the mega railway wagon order been delayed, and what is the plan B?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mega wagon order was expected July-September 2026 but has slipped to next quarter. Plan B is smaller private wagon orders, couplers, suspension tubes, and fabricated loco and metro bogies.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in other expenses, and what is the sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said smaller castings are now outsourced. It guided that sustainable PAT margin is 8-10%, with the current 12% a market-driven high.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of the ~₹100 crore preferential issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about ₹25 crore is for capex and ₹25 crore for working capital, with the remainder for working capital. Capex will not be increased beyond the original plan.

risks_watch: Timing of the mega wagon-bogie order; management says it has slipped to next quarter and remains a key driver of railway volumes.
H2 execution: guidance requires about 50% growth over H1, while fabrication lead times are 3-4 months and working capital is tight until the preferential issue is received.
Commissioning of the fabrication sheds has slipped to Q4 FY27, with spillover into the next FY.
Inventory build-up in H1 FY27 is attributed to inspections; management said it will normalise. Working capital needs rise as volumes move towards ₹500 crore.
Margin sustainability: management called the current margin an anomaly and guided 8-10% PAT margin over the long term.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the headline numbers and FY27 guidance, but cautious on the timing of the railway mega order and the capacity commissioning, which both slipped. Management was direct about margin normalisation, saying 12% PAT is an anomaly and 8-10% is the sustainable range.
key_quotes: This quarter we delivered the highest ever quarterly pact in the company's history.
We have pending orders book as of date also of roughly 150 crores and in pipeline of another 100 plus crores.
Historically for the company even the best of the years has been maximum of 7 to 8 percent that is the history of the company.
I'm sorry to inform you that it has been delayed and now it will be in the next quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H2 EBITDA margin guided broadly similar to H1 at about 19-20% (H1 19.58%, Q2 20.23%), and management called current 12% PAT an anomaly with 8-10% sustainable, so expansion beyond current levels is unlikely while holding steady is the base case.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two of three fabrication sheds expected to complete in FY27 with commissioning guided to Q4 FY27 (slipped from Q3), taking structures capacity from 500 to 1,500 t/month and equipment from 200 to 350 t/month; management said existing capacity covers FY27 volumes.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at ₹300+ crore versus H1 ₹123.96 crore, implying H2 about 50% above H1 with a 40:60 Q3:Q4 split, backed by a ~₹150 crore order book and October plus half of November running ahead of H1 pace.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of ₹25 crore is already planned and four more cocon battery castings batteries (~₹25-30 crore each) are planned next year, with management targeting ₹500 crore revenue in FY28 and current capacity expected at 80-90% utilisation next year.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated ₹300+ crore and said October and half of November ran ahead of H1 pace, but the mega railway order has slipped a quarter, so any upgrade depends on that order landing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guidance needs about 50% H2 growth over H1 while the mega wagon order (30-35k wagons) has slipped to next quarter, fabrication sheds are delayed to Q4 FY27 with about 50% of the project spilling into next FY, and working capital is tight until the ~₹100 crore preferential issue arrives.

rows.label: Mega railway wagon-bogie order slip
rows.why: Order of about 1 lakh wagons (roughly 30-35k wagons) over 2.5-3 years has slipped from July-September 2026 to next quarter; plan B covers couplers, suspension tubes and fabricated bogies, with railways targeted at 30-40% of business.

rows.label: Preferential issue funds working capital
rows.why: About ₹100 crore preferential issue proceeds expected to fund ₹25 crore capex and working capital, which is the main constraint now while working capital needs rise towards the ₹500 crore revenue level.

rows.label: H2 margin normalisation to 8-10% PAT
rows.why: Management called the 12% PAT margin a market-driven high and guided 8-10% sustainable versus a historical 7-8%, with H2 EBITDA margin about 19-20%, held by price-variation clauses in long-term orders.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ₹300+ crore FY27 guidance and H2 margins holding at 19-20%, but cautious on the slipped railway mega order and the fabrication shed commissioning; analysts pushed on how the ~₹60 crore gap to ₹330 crore and working capital would be funded.
